final_message:
I wrote the deviation analysis memo (about 11,200 words). It passes the docx validator and parses back cleanly. Its main finding is that the side letter's own general "side letter controls" sentence does not meet the LPA's test for a side letter overriding the LPA (§ 13.5(b), which requires provision-specific "notwithstanding" wording). Five concessions lack that wording and directly conflict with LPA text: the LPAC seat, automatic Key Person suspension, gross clawback, withdrawal right and, in part, co-investment. The IC memo also gets several terms wrong: co-investment threshold $100M (actual $125M), withdrawal trigger 40% (actual 50%), clawback described as "notwithstanding" (actual "in addition to"), and a $4.5M clawback benefit that is a fund-level figure (PBPEPS's share is about $283K–$289K).
